data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's mechanism depends on all decentralized nodes adhering to one common communication protocol, so a shared protocol bug becomes a correlated trigger. But it explicitly omits the symmetric case from its analysis: the large redundant service also depends on internal protocols, and unless those protocols are different and independently implemented, the same correlated protocol failure can crash every replica at once under identical inputs. Its second countercondition acknowledges this equality ('making it equally susceptible'), which concedes the fault it tries to deny for the large service. It therefore cannot support the comparative resilience claim it asserts for the large service.
